t: Molecular Format Converter - Signature build-tool concept
title: Molecular Format Converter - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Converts between compatible chemical structure formats.
description:
Every build an AI undertakes passes through Molecular Format Converter: Converts between compatible chemical structure formats. The catalog lists it among the thousand fundamental build tools because no serious building happens without it. This database is its Signature edition - the concept rebuilt as a deterministic framework with seven pillars, grounded in real techniques and standards, and taught through a ladder of runnable drills.

The Signature line treats Molecular Format Converter as infrastructure, not inspiration. Infrastructure has contracts: given these inputs, in this state, the Molecular Format Converter produces that output, and anyone can verify it. The seven pillars are those contracts made concrete - each owns one responsibility, each can be tested alone, and together they compose into the full capability. The technique records show the real public knowledge the pillars stand on.

Work through this database the way you would commission a machine: read the charter in the overview, inspect each pillar, check the techniques against your own knowledge, then run the drills. Every record includes a program you can execute with node - the Molecular Format Converter is demonstrated, not merely described.

t: Signature Balancer - Molecular Format Converter framework pillar
title: Signature Balancer - Molecular Format Converter framework pillar
definition: The Balancer component of the Signature Molecular Format Converter framework, owning balancer. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature Molecular Format Converter framework decomposes the capability (Converts between compatible chemical structure formats.) into seven pillars, and the Balancer is the one that owns the framework's balancer responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a Molecular Format Converter result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Balancer's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Balancer's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Molecular Format Converter. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Titrator - Molecular Format Converter framework pillar
title: Signature Titrator - Molecular Format Converter framework pillar
definition: The Titrator component of the Signature Molecular Format Converter framework, owning titrator. Signature concept.
description:
The Titrator is a load-bearing component of the Signature Molecular Format Converter framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's titrator responsibilities belongs to the Titrator, and the Titrator answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Titrator can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Titrator works like this. A build request arrives carrying the Molecular Format Converter charter (converts between compatible chemical structure formats.). The Titrator reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.
